title: Rabbi Huna son of Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Yalkut, Mishlei, remez 961, but the source is Bereshit Rabbah 75:3, and there it is Shmuel bar Nachman. Hyman explains that the abbreviation ר״ה crept in from the preceding line, where it says, “Rav Huna opened; Shmuel bar Nachman said: A parable,” etc.

notes.text: Hyman’s heading fully writes Rabbi Huna, retained in the title. The Midrash Rabbah — TE digital Bereshit Rabbah 75:3 fully writes Rav Huna in the opening, so Rav is used in that quotation. The proposed migration of ר״ה from a preceding line is Hyman’s explanation, not an inspected printing history.

The consulted Yalkut version names Huna son of Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani at the start of the parable. In Bereishit Rabbah, Rav Huna opens and Shmuel bar Nachman tells the parable. Hyman proposes that wording from the preceding line entered the attribution.
